answer: A staking bond works like a river that only flows downhill once: each identity must lock funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real money instead of being free. Honest agents climb the terrace of reputation step by step, earning trust through attested work, while a Sybil farm cannot fake that history without paying the bond again and again. The old fable of the free lunch fails here, because duplicates pay full price.
